properties.name: Census over all 180 tools: the class change this decision asked for exists and needs 173 edits — but about half the sweep's findings belong to no class at all
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-09-11 over all 180 committed toolsnaps, after a sweep that exercised every served tool (430 calls). THIS ANSWERS THE TEST THIS DECISION POSED AND LEFT OPEN. Its own words: *"name a change that WOULD have required editing all 173 tools. If one exists, the factory earns itself."* — and then: **"Posed for tools, it was unanswered."** It is answerable now.

═══ ⭐ THE TEST IS ANSWERED: SEVERAL SUCH CHANGES EXIST ═══

    every tool declares `idempotentHint`              179 edits
    every tool declares `destructiveHint`             173 edits
    every REQUIRED param carries a description         93 edits
    every read-only tool can bound its reply           58 edits
    every caller-assembled payload has a file handle   22 edits

The first two are the decision's OWN axes, still at 1/180 and 7/180 three weeks later. So the answer to *"does a change exist that needs editing across the whole surface"* is yes, it is not hypothetical, and it is the annotation set this node already measured.

═══ THE 2026-08-26 MEASUREMENT, RE-TAKEN — ONE AXIS CLOSED, ONE REGRESSED ═══

    readOnlyHint     161/173 (93%)  →  **180/180 (100%)**
    destructiveHint    7/173        →  7/180
    idempotentHint     1/173        →  1/180
    openWorldHint      0/173        →  0/180
    title              9/173        →  **0/180  ← REGRESSED TO ZERO**

⭐ `readOnlyHint` reaching 100% is the decision's premise confirmed and then some: the read/write class is now universal. It is still **checked by nothing**, so it remains a habit rather than a construction — but a habit at 180/180 is evidence that the cheap end works. `title` going 9 → 0 is the same evidence inverted: an unchecked convention can also decay to nothing, and nobody noticed.

═══ 🛑 AND THE PART THAT ARGUES AGAINST A TAXONOMY ═══

Of roughly thirteen distinct deficiencies the sweep found, **six belong to a class and seven do not.**

CLASS-LEVEL (a fix reaches many):
  · a required param with no description — **93 tools**. This is not abstract: it is why `violates_rule`, `complies_with` and `set_violation_status` declare `rule_id` as a bare string and never say the 27 DesignRules are the wrong type (`fact:the-27-design-rules-are-unreachable-by-the-violation-vocabulary...`).
  · no way to bound a reply — **58 of 68 read-only tools**; seven replies overflowed a client during the sweep.
  · a caller-assembled inline payload with no file handle — **22 tools**.
  · a bare-zero reply that cannot say WHICH empty — see the correlation below.
  · constructors that mint a node from `id` alone — 7 of the 20 `add_*`.
  · acknowledge/withdraw accepting a referent that was never raised — 4 tools.

ONE-OFF (no class fix reaches them): `propose_allocation` returning 238 clusters built on one edge; `reconcile_dependencies` claiming "the build agrees" when no build was observed; `describe_designs` reporting a verified-absent path as `opted_in`; `compose_and_analyse` returning an empty seam because namespacing keeps the two halves apart; `design_regions` exceeding 300 s; `add_interface` unable to state a contract because it shares one request struct with `add_project`; `find_tools` failing to retrieve on a consumer's words.

⚠️ **THAT SPLIT IS THE HONEST ANSWER TO "FIX THE CLASS, NOT THE INSTANCE".** It works for six and buys nothing for seven, which is the counterweight this decision already records in Anthony's own terms — a registry, a factory and a validator is the shape an engineer reaches for, and roughly half these findings would survive it untouched.

═══ THE BARE-ZERO CORRELATION, AND ITS LIMIT ═══

19 of 68 read-only descriptions promise to distinguish an empty answer or name their own blind spot; 49 do not. Median description length: **1,113 chars where it promises, 695 where it does not.** Stronger at the short end — **all 8 read-only tools with descriptions under 65 chars are silent**, and all 7 tools the sweep empirically caught returning an unexplained zero (`hierarchy_issues`, `dimension_drift`, `dimension_drifts`, `mirrors`, `alternatives_for`, `recall_resolutions`, `get_node`) are in that silent set.

🛑 **BUT THE PROXY IS CRUDE AND OVERSTATES ITS CASE.** "Silent" here means a regex over the description found no empty-handling phrase; `loop_status`, `detect_gaps` and `what_next` are flagged silent at ~1,490 chars each and manifestly do handle it. Treat the short end as measured and the long tail as unclassified. **And note the fix is on the REPLY SHAPE, not the description** — rewriting `hierarchy_issues`'s description does not stop it returning `{"count":0,"items":[]}`.

🛑 NOT ESTABLISHED: which classes are WORTH a contract; whether `destructiveHint`/`idempotentHint` would be filled honestly or just filled (this node already names that trap, and `fact:skill-mechanics-track-enforcement-exactly-and-they-split-into-three-kinds` splits mechanics into boilerplate, judgement and tool-side for exactly this reason); and whether a proc-macro surface can carry the exhaustive-match trick that works on a closed enum. No option here is chosen and none was implemented.
